page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured with 2 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB RAM-per-core ratio. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it utilizes a dedicated Intel processor with 1 physical core and 2 threads. The CPU configuration includes a 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It lacks local storage and bundled GPUs, and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate average single-core performance but weak to poor multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU test scored 1554.59 (average), and the Geekbench single-core score reached 1640.0 (average). However, multi-core performance is limited, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 1600.79 (poor) and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2036.0 (weak). Memory bandwidth is also constrained, measuring 15.05 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 9.22 GB/sec for large-block write operations, both falling into the poor category.

This instance is equipped with advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8), which assist in specialized vector and integer operations. Despite these features, its low core count and weak multi-core scaling make it less suitable for parallel processing tasks like software compilation (Geekbench clang score of 2079.0, poor) or database operations (PassMark database score of 931.96, poor). It is best suited for lightweight, memory-bound workloads, basic text processing, or single-threaded applications that require a higher memory-to-vCPU ratio without intensive parallel computational demands.
